## Discovery (lessons from upstream issue #269)

Upstream discovery loops forever when mDNS returns several addresses for one robot (IPv4 from different subnets,
link-local IPv6). Our rules:

- Identify a robot by `GET /api/daemon/hardware-id`, never by IP.
- Store the last successful address; manual IP entry is a first-class feature, not a fallback.
- Show the user which address is in use; provide a force-reconnect action.
- Build URLs with `URLComponents` (brackets IPv6 correctly). Drop `fe80::` link-local candidates unless carrying a
  zone ID.
- Connect must be idempotent and cancellable — no latching state machines.
- Static fallback host: `reachy-mini.local`. Upstream also probes `reachy-mini.home`; do NOT add it back. ATS waives
  its HTTPS requirement only for `.local` names, link-local addresses and single-label hosts, so a qualified `.home`
  name is always refused with `NSURLErrorDomain -1022` — confirmed on a running build. Loopback is probed as well on
  macOS and in the simulator, which is the path that does not depend on discovery working.
- `sim-daemon` **does** advertise `_reachy-mini._tcp`, and a simulator on the same Mac lists it — verified by
  connecting to one from the simulator. A stand-in advert for discovery work is one command:
  `dns-sd -R reachy_mini _reachy-mini._tcp local 8000 unit_id=<hex>`, and a second registration of the same instance
  name comes back as `reachy_mini (2)`.
- An empty discovery list says nothing about the app. Check the robot is actually up first (`ping`, `arp -n <ip>`,
  `dns-sd -B _reachy-mini._tcp`) — a robot that dropped off the network stops advertising, and every layer above
  correctly reports nothing.
- Network change: `NWPathMonitor` + exponential backoff reconnect.

## iOS/iPadOS requirements (app targets)

- `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` + `NSBonjourServices` in Info.plist. Daemon mDNS service types (from upstream
  `src-tauri/src/discovery/mod.rs`): `_reachy-mini._tcp` (primary) and `_http._tcp` (legacy, filter instance names
  containing "reachy") — declare both.
- Local Network permission denial is SILENT: discovery returns an empty list, no error. UX must explain before the
  prompt, detect denial via timeout, and deep-link to Settings.
- ATS: `NSAppTransportSecurity → NSAllowsLocalNetworking: true` — allows plain HTTP to `.local`/link-local only. Never
  use blanket `NSExceptionDomains`.
- The daemon transport is plaintext and unauthenticated. Support only trusted private LANs or the robot AP; show this
  limitation in connection UI and never encourage public routing/port forwarding.

## Robot facts

- Wireless AP mode (out of box): SSID `reachy-mini-ap`, password `reachy-mini`, robot IP `10.42.0.1`.
- BLE Wi-Fi provisioning, daemon 1.9.0+. Upstream doc:

  directly; only daemon-proxied commands notify, after an `OK: working` ack. So: write → read → await a notification
  only if the read was that ack. Awaiting unconditionally hangs on `PING`.
- The robot advertises the **status** service `…cdef3`, not the command service `…cdef0`, under the local name

  CoreBluetooth silently splits a longer value into ATT prepare/execute writes, which the robot then receives as
  separate commands. The command characteristic nevertheless accepts write-with-response only — the write type and
  the size budget are separate questions. Measure both on hardware before building on top of provisioning.
- CoreBluetooth reports a read result and a notification through the same `didUpdateValueFor` callback and offers no
  way to tell them apart. Harmless here: the robot sets the response characteristic's value either way, so a pending
  read may claim whichever arrives.
- `WIFI_SCAN` is truncated to 180 bytes (~8–15 SSIDs, no pagination), so manual SSID entry is mandatory, not a
  fallback. The PIN session dies on disconnect; the wrong-PIN lockout survives it.

[asc] $ ./Scripts/asc.sh publish testflight --help
DESCRIPTION
  Upload and distribute to TestFlight.

USAGE
  asc publish testflight [flags]

Upload or local-build a binary and distribute it to TestFlight beta groups.

Steps:
1. Build locally with Xcode or upload an IPA (unless --build/--build-number is provided)
2. Wait for processing when needed (--wait, --test-notes, or --submit)
3. Add build to specified beta groups
4. Optionally notify testers
5. Optionally submit for beta app review with --submit --confirm

Examples:
  asc publish testflight --app "123" --ipa app.ipa --group "GROUP_ID"
  asc publish testflight --app "123" --workspace App.xcworkspace --scheme App --version 1.2.3 --group "GROUP_ID"
  asc publish testflight --app "123" --ipa app.ipa --group "External Testers"
  asc publish testflight --app "123" --ipa app.ipa --group "G1,G2" --wait --notify
  asc publish testflight --app "123" --ipa app.ipa --group "External Testers" --submit --confirm
  asc publish testflight --app "123" --ipa app.ipa --group "GROUP_ID" --test-notes "Test instructions" --locale "en-US" --wait
  asc publish testflight --app "123" --build "BUILD_ID" --group "GROUP_ID" --wait
  asc publish testflight --app "123" --build-number "42" --group "GROUP_ID" --wait

FLAGS
  --app          App Store Connect app ID (required, or ASC_APP_ID env)
  --archive-path Destination path for the .xcarchive output in local-build mode
  --archive-xcodebuild-flag Pass a raw argument through to xcodebuild during local-build archive (repeatable)
  --build        Existing build ID to distribute (skip upload)
  --build-number CFBundleVersion (used for upload metadata with --ipa, or build lookup when --ipa is omitted)
  --clean        Run clean before local-build archive (default: false)
  --configuration Build configuration for local-build mode (defaults to Release)
  --confirm      Confirm beta app review submission (required with --submit) (default: false)
  --export-options Path to ExportOptions.plist for local-build mode
  --export-xcodebuild-flag Pass a raw argument through to xcodebuild during local-build export (repeatable)
  --group        Beta group ID(s) or name(s), comma-separated
  --initial-build-number Initial build number when local-build mode auto-resolves a build number (default: 1)
  --ipa          Path to .ipa file (required unless --build/--build-number is provided)
  --ipa-path     Destination path for the .ipa output in local-build mode
  --locale       Locale for --test-notes (e.g., en-US)
  --notify       Notify testers after adding to groups (default: false)
  --output       Output format: json, table, markdown (default: table)
  --platform     Platform: IOS, MAC_OS, TV_OS, VISION_OS (default: IOS)
  --poll-interval Polling interval for --wait and build discovery (default: 30s)
  --pretty       Pretty-print JSON output (default: false)
  --project      Path to .xcodeproj directory for local-build mode
  --scheme       Xcode scheme name for local-build mode
  --submit       Submit build for beta app review after adding external groups (default: false)

#!/bin/bash
# Run the App Store Connect CLI against the release credentials.
#
#   mise run asc -- apps list
#   mise run asc -- builds list --app 6799644194
#
# The three values asc wants are the three release.env already carries, under
# other names — so nothing is stored twice and no keychain profile is created.
# asc resolves a stored profile first and falls back to the environment, which
# means a hand-made `asc auth login` keeps winning over this wrapper.
set -euo pipefail

# shellcheck source=Scripts/release-env.sh
. "$(dirname "$0")/release-env.sh"
require_asc_key

export ASC_KEY_ID="$REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID"
export ASC_ISSUER_ID="$REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID"
export ASC_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH="$REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH"
# Piped output is JSON either way; this only decides what a terminal shows.
export ASC_DEFAULT_OUTPUT="${ASC_DEFAULT_OUTPUT:-table}"

exec asc "$@"

As of 2026-08-11 there is no Apple ID signed into Xcode on this machine —
`defaults read com.apple.dt.Xcode` shows
`DVTDeveloperAccountManagerAppleIDLists → IDE.Identifiers.Prod = ()`, an empty
list. Signing certificates are still in the keychain, so archiving and a local
export both succeed; only the legs that need the *account* fail:

- iOS `-exportArchive` with `destination: upload` → `Failed to Use Accounts`,
  and the distribution log names the step: `IDEDistributionUploadAccountStep`,
  "Failed to find an account with App Store Connect access for team J52C3SB8K5".
- macOS App Store export → `No Accounts` plus
  `No signing certificate "Mac Installer Distribution" found`; that certificate
  does not exist on the account at all (`asc certificates list` shows only
  DEVELOPER_ID_APPLICATION, DISTRIBUTION and two DEVELOPMENT), because
  `-allowProvisioningUpdates` is what used to create it through the account.

**Why:** `Scripts/release-env.sh` deliberately withholds the ASC API key from
`xcodebuild` (an App Manager key turns the flags into cloud signing, which it is
not entitled to do), so the upload leg has no credential to fall back on.

**How to apply:** for iOS, export locally instead of uploading — copy
`Scripts/exportOptions/appstore.plist`, `plutil -replace destination -string export`,
run `-exportArchive` against the existing archive — then
`asc publish testflight --app 6799644194 --ipa "…/Hey Reachy.ipa" --group <id>
--test-notes … --locale en-US --wait --submit --confirm`, which uploads with the
same key and attaches the public group in one call. macOS App Store has no such
detour: it needs a Mac Installer Distribution certificate, so either sign back
into Xcode (Settings → Accounts) or mint the certificate through
`asc certificates create --certificate-type MAC_INSTALLER_DISTRIBUTION --generate-csr`
plus a Mac App Store profile. See [[asc-cli-wiring]], [[verify-testflight-upload]],
[[device-build-signing]].

  DEVELOPER_ID_APPLICATION, DISTRIBUTION and two DEVELOPMENT), because
  `-allowProvisioningUpdates` is what used to create it through the account.

**Why:** `Scripts/release-env.sh` deliberately withholds the ASC API key from
`xcodebuild` (an App Manager key turns the flags into cloud signing, which it is
not entitled to do), so the upload leg has no credential to fall back on.

**How to apply:** for iOS, export locally instead of uploading — copy
`Scripts/exportOptions/appstore.plist`, `plutil -replace destination -string export`,
run `-exportArchive` against the existing archive — then
`asc publish testflight --app 6799644194 --ipa "…/Hey Reachy.ipa" --group <id>
--test-notes … --locale en-US --wait --submit --confirm`, which uploads with the
same key and attaches the public group in one call. macOS App Store has no such
detour: it needs a Mac Installer Distribution certificate, so either sign back
into Xcode (Settings → Accounts) or mint the certificate through
`asc certificates create --certificate-type MAC_INSTALLER_DISTRIBUTION --generate-csr`
plus a Mac App Store profile. See [[asc-cli-wiring]], [[verify-testflight-upload]],

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **Корень обеих неудач один:** `defaults read com.apple.dt.Xcode` показывает `DVTDeveloperAccountManagerAppleIDLists → IDE.Identifiers.Prod = ()` — в Xcode **не залогинен ни один Apple ID**. Сертификаты в связке ключей живут отдельно от аккаунта, поэтому архив и локальный экспорт проходят, а всё, что идёт «через аккаунт» (аплоад, автосоздание Mac Installer Distribution), — нет.
- **`asc publish testflight` заменяет сразу три шага из `docs/release.md`**: аплоад по API-ключу, привязку к публичной группе и подачу на Beta App Review — одной командой, плюс `--test-notes`. Это тот же ключ, что уже лежит в `release.env`, так что обходной путь не потребовал новых секретов.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Готово

**0.1.2 выпущен.**

| Шаг | Статус |
| --- | --- |
| `MARKETING_VERSION` 0.1.1 → 0.1.2, коммит `0c47394` на `main` | ✅ CI зелёный (4m33s) |
| Тег `0.1.2` + GitHub-релиз с заметками git-cliff | ✅ [релиз](https://github.com/alexey1312/reachy-mini-swift/releases/tag/0.1.2) |
| iOS: архив, проверка App Intents (8 actions, 6 shortcuts) | ✅ |
| iOS → TestFlight, сборка **122**, `VALID` | ✅ |
| iOS → публичная группа + Beta App Review | ✅ `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW` |
| «What to Test» (en-US) | ✅ |
| macOS: архив, нотаризация (`Accepted`), staple | ✅ |
| macOS Developer ID zip в GitHub-релизе (24.5 МБ) | ✅ `spctl: accepted` |
| **macOS → TestFlight** | ❌ заблокировано |

## Что не доехало и почему

macOS App Store канал упал на экспорте:

```
exportArchive No Accounts
exportArchive No signing certificate "Mac Installer Distribution" found
```

Сертификата `Mac Installer Distribution` нет ни в связке ключей, ни на аккаунте — `asc certificates list` знает только `DEVELOPER_ID_APPLICATION`, `DISTRIBUTION` и два `DEVELOPMENT`. Раньше его автоматически создавал `-allowProvisioningUpdates` через аккаунт Xcode, а аккаунта сейчас нет. По той же причине сегодня отвалился и iOS-аплоад — его я обошёл через `asc`, но для `.pkg` обхода нет: без установочного сертификата пакет просто нечем подписать.

Архив macOS (`Apps/DerivedData/Archives/ReachyMini-macOS.xcarchive`, версия 0.1.2, билд 122) лежит готовый — доделать можно одной командой, но развилка ваша:

1. **Залогиниться в Xcode** → Settings → Accounts → добавить Apple ID (нужен 2FA, поэтому за вас не сделаю). Дальше — `mise run release:macos -- --channel appstore`, и это же чинит штатный путь для всех будущих релизов.
2. **Выписать сертификат по API** — `asc certificates create --certificate-type MAC_INSTALLER_DISTRIBUTION --generate-csr`, импорт ключа в связку, плюс Mac App Store профиль через `asc profiles create`. Работает без GUI, но заводит на вашем developer-аккаунте подписные ресурсы в обход того, что описано в `docs/release.md` — поэтому спрашиваю, а не делаю молча.

Скажите, какой вариант — доведу macOS до публичной группы тем же способом, что и iOS.

Отдельно: релиз собран как патч (0.1.1 → 0.1.2), хотя между тегами шесть `feat`-коммитов, включая шесть тем оформления и виджет — по семверу это тянуло на 0.2.0. Сделал как просили; если хотите перевыпустить как минорный, скажите.

security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 reachy-signing.keychain
